title: A renamed part's core takes the same part number
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test with a Core Charge of $15.00, so it has a core.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. Click the part A row.
  2. Replace the Part Number with the new number.
  3. Click Save.
  4. Open the core's own Part History page.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 2:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 3:

  • The window closes and part A's row shows the new number.

Step 4:

  • The core's own Part History page shows the new number as its part number.
  • Its newest entry reads "Part number updated | Original number:" with the old number, then "| New number:" with the new number: the core took the same number.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog), story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change), story SV-10818 (Story 5, Change Tracking on an Existing Part)

  • S13-R18: “Saving a changed number renames the part in place. The part keeps its identity, its history, and every line that holds it. Its Part Library entry is renamed with it, and its core takes the same number. No new Part Library entry is created.”
  • S10-R26: “When the part has a core, the core gets the same number or description entry. The core's description entries read its own description, "Core for {description}".”
  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
